subject.title: fix(autoreview): allow safe Python runtime references

question: Is the new Python runtime-expression allowlist and stricter Testbox temp-root ownership policy narrow enough to become part of autoreview's trust boundary?
rationale: Tests establish the intended cases, but deciding which source expressions may bypass secret-like assignment findings and which shared temp roots are trusted requires human security-policy judgment.

options.title: Approve the bounded rules
options.body: Accept the parser and ownership checks after an area-owner review confirms every allowlisted grammar form fails closed.

options.title: Narrow before merge
options.body: Reduce accepted Python shapes or split the temp-root policy if either change is broader than the immediate reproduction requires.

options.title: Keep strict rejection
options.body: Preserve current scanner behavior and require downstream code to avoid secret-like binding names.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded rules
recommendation.body: Accept the parser and ownership checks after an area-owner review confirms every allowlisted grammar form fails closed.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history shows concentrated ownership of the credential scanner and its hardening tests.
